general_policy.user_quote: [English translation] Use the upstream implementation as much as possible and add our fixes where it makes sense.
general_policy.rule: Use upstream as the base as much as possible; preserve all missing Joom capabilities, fixes and optimizations. If behavior or optimization is lost, retain/adapt our part.
conditions: Confirm functional equivalence through Joom regressions and actual native execution/plan checks.

For optimizations, verify memory/spill lifecycle and perform available local performance measurements where possible; explicitly identify unverified performance. Full GCP benchmarks are deferred to user validation.
A partial equivalent does not imply a complete replacement of the Joom capability.
Do not exclude Joom behavior merely because upstream has a similar mechanism.

I01.decision: Use the Comet1.2 native Delta scanner; preserve GCP ADC, serialization and planning-deadlock protection, adapting missing Joom specifics.

D10.decision: Use upstream Single/Final+MergeAsPartial and new Spark aggregate-state codecs; preserve spill robustness and port Joom memory/offset guards, ordered drain and low-copy collect_list. Do not port old Joom PartialReduce routing unless necessary.

N08.decision: Preserve upstream SortAggregate architecture and add missing Joom ordering/streaming optimizations and required correctness guards.

I06.decision: Use upstream timestamp producer/CASE fixes and Spark4.2 semantics; port our additional comparison normalization where still necessary.

I07.decision: Use upstream native wide-decimal hashing instead of restoring the old precision>18 restriction; verify Spark compatibility, including mixed boundaries.

N06.decision: Use upstream native string MIN/MAX; preserve Joom cases, native coverage and missing guards.

I04.decision: Use the upstream DPP/empty-scan lifecycle; preserve corresponding Joom regressions and missing fixes.

I05.decision: Use upstream recursive boolean FFI repair; preserve additional Joom nested/sliced regressions.

J18.decision: Use upstream one-time bundled native-library loading; verify the original Joom reload scenario.

J21.decision: Use upstream sliced-broadcast offset normalization; retain Joom regressions and add missing fixes if behavior is lost.

J24.decision: Use the upstream small-batch/effective JVM shuffle batch cap; preserve our checks.

P03.decision: Keep ANSI=true. Prioritize preventing successful jobs with incorrect results. Compare Spark4.2.1 Comet-off/on with identical inputs/ANSI; verify results and mandatory errors; preserve SUM/AVG overflow guards, fix incompatibilities or restrict the native path before execution. Add automated regression/differential tests during implementation where possible. Do not include PR#5889 in this migration.

I03.decision: Preserve planning-deadlock protection through the current upstream lifecycle with the correct execution partition count; do not copy the old unconditional UnknownPartitioning(0). Verify the original Joom reproductions.

J09.decision: Preserve the Joom projection-instance pool on top of upstream generated-class caching, respecting lifetime/bounds guards. A partial class cache alone does not replace the pool; simplify only with demonstrated equivalence under the approved rule.

ansi_policy.rule: The target Spark4.2.1 mode is ANSI=true. Fix confirmed incompatibilities or restrict the corresponding native path before execution; do not globally disable ANSI to work around differences.

correctness_policy.priority: Prevent a job from completing without error and publishing an incorrect result.
correctness_policy.user_quote: [English translation] Above all, we must do everything we can to prevent a job from completing without error while producing an incorrect result.
release_criteria: Known unsafe native paths are fixed or excluded through planning-time fallback before execution; green job/CI status alone is insufficient.
Compare Spark4.2.1 without and with Comet on the same input snapshot, identical ANSI=true and other relevant settings.
Compare actual results, types, NULL, duplicate rows and guaranteed SQL order; do not rely only on count or individual sums.
Check both sides of the contract: must succeed/must fail. Comet success where Spark requires an ANSI error is a correctness violation.
Preserve overflow detection and guards for mixed Spark/native partial-final SUM/AVG, including the new state codec.
For a confirmed incompatibility, select fallback before execution/publication; do not rely on retry in Spark after writing or an error.
Verify actual native execution/plans so fallback does not hide lack of testing of the custom path.
Do not hide differences with general normalization, loss of duplicates or arbitrary float tolerances; respect defined Spark semantics and permitted nondeterminism.
correctness_policy.automated_regressions: Add automated regression/differential tests during implementation where possible; this step records the plan without writing code.
priority_cases: Mixed Spark/native decimal SUM/AVG and intermediate overflow, forced spill and the new PartialMerge codec.
Separately test runtime-codegen-fallback decimal SUM; static NO_CODEGEN guards are insufficient.
Grouped decimal AVG+LIMIT, malformed casts, arithmetic overflow, division by zero and lazy AND/OR/CASE/JVM dispatch.
SMJ hoisting: can-throw expressions/conditional branches/outer join, ANSI=true.
Custom RANGE windows at DATE/DECIMAL boundaries and existing fallback guards.
Results with active Joom cost/boundary flags, mixed shuffle, AQE on/off; native-plan checks.
Known silent-result edge cases regardless of ANSI, including BINARY→STRING/invalidUTF8 where applicable.
correctness_policy.limits: A test suite is not a mathematical proof that all bugs are absent. Explicitly record uncovered risks; do not claim compatibility proven without validation.
